title: Feature/playlist editor redesign
summary: This redesigns how playlists are made and played. On a computer, creating or editing a playlist now opens a fullscreen editor with the steps on the left, the open step in the middle and its settings on the right, plus a new "Add a step" window and a "Review & publish" screen. Playlists can now hold scenes, notes on passages, questions, side-by-side compares and videos; non-scripture steps play on their own fullscreen screen; a shared session gets a "party mode" where the leader moves everyone on; and there's a new completion screen and a "Continue your playlist" card on Today. The pull request has no description, so the tests below follow what the app does.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the window at full width. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email: Seed Bible emails you a code, so you need an inbox you can check. Saving and publishing a playlist needs an account.

setup.title: Find the Discover pane
setup.body: Open **Discover** from the app's menu. This is where playlists are listed, created and played. Every test below starts from here unless it says otherwise.

sections.title: Making a playlist on a computer
sections.intro: The new fullscreen editor, used on any screen wider than a phone.

tests.title: Creating a playlist opens the fullscreen editor
tests.why: The main new screen of this pull request.
steps: In **Discover**, choose **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
Type `Test playlist` in the **Playlist title** box at the top.
expected: The editor fills the screen, with three columns: **Steps** on the left, a message saying "Pick a step on the left, or add one." in the middle, and **Step settings** on the right ("Select a step to see its settings.").
Under the title it says **Draft · not saved yet** or **Draft · unsaved changes**.
Along the top are **Edit** / **Preview** buttons, **Test with a group** and **Review & publish**.

tests.title: Add a scripture step by typing a reference
tests.before: Keep the editor from the previous test open.
steps: Choose **Add step** at the bottom of the Steps column.
In the **Add a step** window, leave **Scripture** selected under "1 · Step type".
Under "2 · Passage", type `John 3:16-18`.
Choose **Add step**.
expected: While you type, the window shows the chapter's verses with 16–18 marked, and the bottom of the window says something like "Scripture · John 3:16-18 · 3 verses".
The window closes and **John 3:16-18** appears as step 1 in the Steps column, opened in the middle column.
The Steps column heading shows the step count and an estimated time (for example "1 · ~1 min").

tests.title: Pick a passage by dragging across verses
steps: Choose **Add step** again, keep **Scripture**.
Type `Psalm 23` so the chapter's text shows, then press and drag from verse 1 to verse 3 in the text.
Choose **Add step**.
expected: The dragged verses are selected and the reference box updates to Psalm 23:1-3.
Step 2 is added after step 1.

tests.title: Add one of each other step type
tests.why: Note, Note + Scripture, Compare, Video, Question and Link are all new or reworked step types.
steps: Add a **Note** step: choose **Add step**, pick **Note**, type `A short note for readers`, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Note + Scripture** step: pick it, type the passage `Romans 8:28`, type a note title and a short note, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Compare** step: pick it, enter `Genesis 1:1` and `John 1:1` as the two passages, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Question** step: pick it, type `What stood out to you?`, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Link** step with the address `https://example.com`.
Add a **Video** step with any YouTube video address, and leave the **Transcript** box empty.
expected: Each type's window shows the right fields (a writing box for Note, a passage plus note for Note + Scripture, two passages for Compare, a question box for Question, an address box for Link and Video).
Each new step appears in the Steps column with an icon or label that matches its type, numbered in order.

tests.title: Add a scene and see steps grouped under it
steps: Choose **Add scene** at the bottom of the Steps column.
With the scene open in the middle, give it the title `Scene 1 · Beginnings`.
Drag the scene to the top of the list, or add it before your other steps.
expected: The scene shows as a heading ("Scene 1 · Beginnings") with the steps after it grouped underneath, and it can be collapsed and expanded.
Scenes don't take a step number: the steps keep numbering 1, 2, 3…
With the scene open, Step settings says "A scene is a heading over the steps after it." and offers **Delete scene**.

tests.title: Step settings: reading time, group options and changing type
steps: Open step 1 (John 3:16-18) in the Steps column.
Under **Reading time**, note the estimate and the word "auto", then choose **edit**, type `5`, and press Enter.
Choose **Use the estimate**.
Tick **Leader only (hide from solo readers)** and **Pause here for discussion**.
Under **Type**, choose **Note + Scripture**.
expected: After typing 5, reading time shows 5 min and the Steps column's total time goes up. **Use the estimate** puts it back to the estimate with "auto".
The ticks stay ticked when you open another step and come back.
Choosing a different type opens a window titled **Change the step's type**; after you finish it, the step keeps its place, its reading time and both ticks.

tests.title: Same passage twice in a row is flagged
steps: Add a new **Scripture** step for exactly the same passage as the step before it (for example `Psalm 23:1-3` right after Psalm 23:1-3).
Look at **Step settings** for the new step.
Choose **Remove step N** in the warning.
expected: A warning says "Same passage as step N" and "Readers will see Psalm 23:1-3 twice in a row. This step already shows it."
**Remove step N** removes the earlier copy, and the warning goes away.
Note for testers: "Keep both" next to it is plain text, not a button. Say in your notes whether that seems right.

tests.title: Edit a step in place and see it in Preview
steps: Open the **Note** step and change its text.
Without saving anything else, choose **Preview** at the top.
Choose **Edit** again, then open the Note + Scripture step and try the note editor's extras: select a word and use **Link to verse**, **Link to step** and **Embed passage**.
expected: Preview shows the open step the way readers will see it, including your changed text.
The draft line at the top says **Draft · unsaved changes**.
A word linked to a verse or step shows as a link in the note; an embedded passage shows the verse text inside the note.

tests.title: Leaving with unsaved changes asks first
steps: Change the text of any open step but don't move to another step.
Choose the back arrow (‹) at the top left of the editor.
expected: A dialog asks what to do with your unsaved changes instead of closing straight away. Choose the option that keeps your work, so later tests can use this playlist.

tests.title: The review screen lists checks and how the playlist appears
tests.before: Use the playlist from the previous section. It should include a Video step with no transcript.
steps: Choose **Review & publish**.
Read the **Before you publish** list.
Choose **Add one** (or **Fix**) next to the video transcript line.
expected: The screen shows Title, Description, Cover, **Who can open it** (Only me / Anyone with the link / Public in Discover) and a **How it appears** card with the step and scene counts.
**Before you publish** includes lines such as "All passages found in …", a count of notes/questions/linked phrases, and "Video in step N has no transcript."
**Add one** takes you back to the editor with the video step open, where a **Transcript** box is available.

tests.title: Publish as "Anyone with the link" and find it again
steps: Add a transcript to the video step, then choose **Review & publish** again.
Under **Who can open it**, choose **Anyone with the link**.
Choose **Publish**.
Go back to **Discover** and find `Test playlist`, then open its options and choose **Edit playlist**.
expected: The button briefly says **Saving…**, then the editor closes and the playlist is saved.
The playlist appears in your list; editing it reopens the fullscreen editor with every step, scene and setting as you left them, and the draft line says **Draft · saved** with a time.

tests.title: Publish is blocked for an empty playlist
steps: Start a new playlist (**+ Create**, **Playlist**), add only a scene, and choose **Review & publish**.
expected: **Before you publish** says "Add at least one step before publishing." and the **Publish** button can't be pressed.
Leave this playlist without saving it.

sections.title: Playing a playlist on your own

tests.title: Scripture steps play in the reader with the playlist beside it
steps: In **Discover**, open `Test playlist` and choose **Play playlist**.
Go to a scripture step (John 3:16-18).
expected: The side panel shows "Playlist · By <your name>" and the title, a progress bar, "Step N of M" and the current step highlighted in the queue.
The reader shows the passage, marked as the playing passage, with an **End of passage** marker after the last verse and a button for the next step ("Next · …").
The step you marked **Leader only** is not in the queue when playing alone.

tests.title: Note, link, question and compare steps fill the screen
steps: Continue to the Note step, then the Question, Compare and Link steps, using **Next step**.
On the Question step, type an answer in **Your response** and choose **Save response**.
On the Compare step, try **Open <passage> in a tab**.
expected: These steps take over the reading area with a header ("Playlist · By … · N steps · ~X min"), a segmented progress bar, an eyebrow like "Note · Step 3 of 8 · 1 min", **Previous** and **Next step** buttons, and an "Up next" line.
Saving the answer shows "Saved to your profile."
Compare shows both passages side by side; the tab button opens that passage in a new tab.
The close (×) button stops playing and returns to the reader.

tests.title: Listen reads scripture steps aloud
steps: While playing, choose the headphones button (**Listen**) in the Discover pane header.
Move to a scripture step that doesn't start at verse 1.
expected: The button shows as on (**Listening**) and narration starts at the passage's first verse, not at the start of the chapter.
Pressing it again turns listening off.

tests.title: Finishing shows the completion screen
steps: Go to the last step and choose **Finish** (or **Finish playlist**).
expected: A **Playlist complete** screen shows how many steps and passages you went through and a **What you read** list, with **Share playlist** and **Done** buttons.
**Share playlist** copies the link and says so.

tests.title: Today offers to continue an unfinished playlist
steps: Play `Test playlist` again and stop part-way through (close the player on step 2 or 3).
Open **Today**.
Choose **Resume**.
expected: Today shows a **Continue your playlist** card with the title, "Step N of M" and the step you were on.
**Resume** opens the playlist at that step, and only then closes Today.
After finishing the playlist, the card no longer appears on Today.

sections.title: Playing with a group (party mode)
sections.intro: Needs two browsers or two devices.

setup.title: Prepare a second browser
setup.body: Open the preview link in a second browser, or a private/incognito window, signed in with a different account (or signed out, if joining a session allows it).

setup.title: Start a session
setup.body: In the first browser, choose **Share**, then **Start and share session**, and open the copied link in the second browser so both are in the same session. The first browser is the leader.

tests.title: The leader moves everyone; others say they're ready
steps: In the leader's browser, play `Test playlist` inside the session.
In the second browser, choose **I'm ready**.
In the leader's browser, choose **Move everyone to step N**.
expected: The leader's header says **Live · You're leading**; the other says **Live · Following <leader's name>**.
The ready count updates on both screens (for example "1 of 1 ready") and the chat says "Everyone is ready to move on".
Both browsers move to the next step, and the chat shows "<name> moved everyone to step N · <title>".
The **Leader only** step is part of the queue in the session.

tests.title: Shared answers and comments on verses
steps: On the Question step, in the second browser, write an answer, choose **Session** under **Who can see this**, and save it.
On a scripture step, in either browser, select a verse in the reader and choose **Comment in session** from the verse tools.
In the other browser, choose **Jump to verse** on that chat message.
expected: The leader sees the answer under **Group answers** ("1 shared"), and the chat shows "shared an answer" with "Asked: What stood out to you?".
The comment appears in the session chat attached to the verse (or phrase), and **Jump to verse** takes the reader there.

tests.title: Test with a group plays an unsaved draft
steps: In the leader's browser, edit `Test playlist` and change a step without publishing.
Choose **Test with a group**.
expected: A shared session starts on a new tab and the draft plays there, including the unsaved change, so others can join with **Invite**.

sections.title: On a phone
sections.intro: Use a real phone, or make the browser window narrower than 480 pixels.

tests.title: The phone editor is one column and still edits steps in place
steps: In **Discover**, choose **+ Create**, **Playlist**.
Use **Add item** to add a scripture step and a note, then choose **Done**.
Tap a step to edit it, change it, and tap away before saving.
expected: Instead of the fullscreen editor, a single column shows Cover image, Description, **Who can open it**, the numbered steps, **Add item** and **Add scene**.
Each step's editor opens inside its own row.
Leaving a changed step without saving shows **Unsaved item changes** with **Discard changes** and **Keep changes and save**.

tests.title: The phone player sheet
steps: Play `Test playlist` on the phone.
Use the sheet's button to fold the step away, then show it again.
expected: A sheet at the bottom shows the current step and an "Up next · …" line, with a **Listen** button.
Folding hides the step so the reader is visible; showing it brings it back. Nothing is cut off at the screen edges.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Reading plan editor still works, with items edited in place
steps: Open **Reading plans**, create or edit a reading plan, and add a scripture reading.
Use the reading's **Edit** button to change it, then save the plan.
expected: The reading opens for editing in place (the button is labeled "Edit <reading>", where it used to say "Preview"), and the change is saved.

tests.title: Older playlists still open and play
steps: Open a playlist that was made before this change (one of yours, or one in Discover) and play it from start to finish.
expected: Every step plays, nothing is missing or shown as an unknown type, and the completion screen appears at the end.

tests.title: Dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode and look at the fullscreen editor, the Add a step window, the Review & publish screen and a fullscreen Note step.
expected: All text is readable, with no white boxes or invisible text.

notCovered: The large set of new automated tests that came with this change.
The **Pause here for discussion** setting is saved with a step, but nothing in playback appears to use it yet, so there's nothing to check beyond the tick staying ticked.
Translated (non-English) text: only the English wording was added, and translators will fill in the rest later.
